What is the best part of KY and what is the worst part of KY in your opinion?

West Kentucky is obviously the best, although I may be a little biased. Paducah is very quaint and historic. We also have Land Between the Lakes, which is a huge tourist spot and a wonderful place to hike and camp. In addition, the countryside is beautiful, and we're near both of the country's main rivers. They combine a few miles away in Illinois.
I wouldn't say there's a 'worst part', but Appalachia usually gets made fun of the most. Poverty is extremely common in most of the state, however. Louisville, Lexington, and the central countryside are the most popular sites in Kentucky. Churchill Downs, tobacco and horse racing are what most of the country thinks of when they hear Kentucky. Most of that is located there.

What is the general feeling about East Asians? Is there a general level of racism against them?

I'll give you another perspective on another part of KY. We have a Thai population and they are beloved. They are relentless workers, and have taken distressed old fast food restaurants and have turned them into valuable properties, and prospering businesses which everyone loves. They are beloved. We also have many Japanese businesses and have a pretty significant Asian population in this part of KY with Mazak etc..

My dad was in the Army when allot of the South Vietnamese were brought over and were given free housing in barracks at Ft Knox (Louisville area), and Ft Campbell (Southern Border). He still talks about the Vietnamese being such great people and how they were all integrated into society within a year and had no government type handouts really. They were so smart and hardworking that they all started businesses and integrated with hardly any government assistance and how much he respected them and how all the housing that he built went vacant.
